answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a reputation bond earned slowly through verifiable work, not bought in bulk. Like a dune shaped grain by grain, trust accumulates over many completed tasks, while a basalt foundation of on-chain attestations from established peers anchors each agent. New identities start with velvet-soft privileges: they can observe and take small jobs, but cannot vote or move large value until their history proves they are distinct, costly to fake, and consistent over time.
